compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

Most plan-review criteria have no eval fixture, so a rubric edit ships with no behavioral
oracle. Something must first decide which observed reviews are trustworthy evidence of a
criterion's behavior — the corpus records what the reviewer said, not what was true.

Two hazards make naive selection wrong. Reviewer noise: 551 consecutive review pairs over
byte-identical material flipped verdict 208 times, so one observation is not a label. Prompt
vintage: rubrics were rewritten repeatedly inside the corpus window, so a finding from a
retired rubric does not describe today's criterion, and nothing cohorts by vintage — `regver`
(`manifest.py:139-185`) hashes routing and ids, not rubric bytes. `plan_replay/corpus.py`
reconstructs each row's at-review plan text (`corpus.py:270-288`) over the 6,482 committed
rows in `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/replay/corpus-2026-08-30.manifest.json`.

## Approach

An offline selector that reads the corpus and writes a LABELED CANDIDATE MANIFEST — per
criterion, each candidate with its direction, tier, signals and rank, plus a row for every
criterion that produced none, with the reason. It emits no YAML and issues no model call.

**Candidate key and signal join.** A candidate is keyed by `(criterion, norm_id)`
(`sidecar.py:656,663`); signals join on that key across a ticket's review sequence. This is
load-bearing because the two signals live on different pair relationships: `labels.py`
computes `finding_survival` only over consecutive DIFFERING-material pairs, while
reproduction consensus is defined over EQUAL-`material_fingerprint` pairs. The selector reads
consensus from the equal-fingerprint reviews carrying the key, and author-response from the
first differing-material pair after the last of those; a key in only one relationship gets
only that signal.

**Vintage gate.** A review is eligible for criterion C only when `review_event_ts`
(`corpus.py:273`) postdates the last `origin/main` commit touching C's rubric file. The
selector does NOT hand-build that path — a built-in's prompt id is hyphenated while its
packaged filename is underscored (`prompts.py:162`), so a hand-built path matches nothing.
With `pid = criterion_prompt_id(C)` it mirrors `get_prompt`'s own override-wins ordering
(`prompts.py:187-198`): git-log `.rebar/prompts/<pid>.md` when that file exists, else
`reviewers/` joined to the `fallback_file` of `prompts.get_prompt(pid)`. The override path
must be tested directly because `get_prompt` sets `fallback_file` only to the PACKAGED name
(`prompts.py:196`) and never exposes the override it read.

A criterion whose resolved file has no `origin/main` history — an uncommitted override, or a
rubric added after the corpus was frozen — FAILS the gate and is recorded as a zero-candidate
row with reason `no-committed-prompt-history`. The gate turns on git history alone, never on
the criterion's name. A signal read from the Pass-2 vector additionally requires postdating
the file resolved the same way for prompt id `plan-review-verifier`.

**Label signals**, offline and independent of the reviewer's own verdict:
- *Reproduction consensus* — the key fired, or stayed absent, consistently across two or more
  reviews with equal `material_fingerprint`. The only signal valid in the no-fire direction.
- *Author response* — `finding_survival == "resolved_by_author"` (`labels.py:158-171`), the
  only per-finding label the labels module produces. Fire direction only.

**Escaped defect is a PRIORITY signal, not a label.** `labels.py:70-73` derives
`escaped_defect` from a ticket's `close_class` and inbound `caused_by` links — a per-TICKET
bool with no criterion attribution, so using it as a label would seed a must-fire candidate
under an unrelated criterion. It only raises a review's rank. Its absence never evidences
correct silence, so `clean_close` (`labels.py:43`) is not a no-fire source.

**Tiered bar.** The vintage gate is a precondition of BOTH tiers: a candidate failing it is
excluded, not downgraded. Among those that pass, a FIRE candidate is BLOCKING only when all
three hold: reproduction consensus, author-response corroboration, and `abs(decision_margin)`
(`sidecar.py:344-367`) at or above the constant `MIN_MARGIN = 0.15`. Those latter two are
per-finding and exist only in the fire direction, so a NO-FIRE candidate reaches at most
ADVISORY, on consensus alone. Any single signal proposes ADVISORY. The margin constant drops
findings close enough to `block_threshold` that a small perturbation flips them.

**Rank order.** BLOCKING before ADVISORY, then escaped-defect priority, then descending
`abs(decision_margin)`, then ascending `review_event_uuid` as a total tie-break, so the
emitter takes a fixed number per side deterministically.

**Skip list.** A criterion with an open ticket titled `unreliable-criterion: <criterion-id>`
is skipped and recorded as a zero-candidate row with that reason.

## Scope

A new module under `src/rebar/llm/evals/` holding the selector, its predicates and the
manifest writer, over `plan_replay/corpus.py` and `plan_replay/labels.py`. It covers only
criteria `criteria.effective_routing('.', gate_key='plan_review')` reports with no spec under
`.rebar/evals/` or `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/`.

## Non-goals

- Writing any `.eval.yaml`, or admitting a candidate; the sibling emitter and the admission
  runner own those.
- Any model call.
- Per-finding true/false-positive labelling or human adjudication.

## Testing

Unit tests over the predicates on synthetic corpus rows, plus one integration test over the
real corpus with no model configured; all assertions are deterministic.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A review predating its criterion's resolved rubric commit is excluded and an
      otherwise-identical later one included; verified by `pytest` asserting the manifest
      holds the second row's id, not the first's.
- [ ] The gate git-logs `.rebar/prompts/<pid>.md` for a criterion carrying an override and
      the packaged `fallback_file` for one without; verified by `pytest` asserting the
      queried path in both cases.
- [ ] A criterion excluded for either reason — no `origin/main` rubric history, or an open
      `unreliable-criterion: <id>` ticket — carries a zero-candidate row naming that reason;
      verified by parameterized `pytest` over an uncommitted override and a stubbed listing.
- [ ] A fire candidate failing the vintage gate produces no candidate row rather than an
      advisory one; verified by `pytest` asserting its absence from the candidate list.
- [ ] Removing each of reproduction consensus, author-response and margin in turn downgrades
      a fire candidate to `advisory`, while all three present yields `blocking`; verified by
      parameterized `pytest` over the recorded tier.
- [ ] A no-fire candidate never reaches `blocking`; verified by `pytest` asserting `advisory`
      for one holding reproduction consensus.
- [ ] A candidate whose only signal is `escaped_defect` appears in no direction, while one
      carrying it outranks an equal-signal peer; verified by `pytest` asserting the candidate
      list and the two ranks.
- [ ] A key present only in equal-fingerprint pairs records reproduction consensus and no
      author-response signal; verified by `pytest` asserting the recorded signal set.
- [ ] Given 6 qualifying candidates on one side with distinct margins, the recorded ranks
      follow the stated order; verified by `pytest` over the rank sequence.
- [ ] Two consecutive real runs over the committed corpus emit a byte-identical manifest, and
      the run completes under the repository's network guard; verified by `diff` of the two
      files exiting 0 with the guard active.

## Definition of Done

`make lint`, `make typecheck` and `make test` pass; the real-corpus run writes a manifest row
for every uncovered criterion; `.rebar/evals/` is untouched.

## Budget

**$0.** Selection is a pure function of the corpus and git metadata.
